title: RBAC permissions for route experiment actions (create/start/stop/update/delete + debug access)
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
Problem
- Route experiments add a new mutation surface area in Console (create/update/start/stop/delete; ramp traffic splits; set guardrails) that must be permissioned consistently across Hosted/Dedicated/Private customers.
- Enterprise customers require least-privilege roles and demonstrable auditability: who changed what, when, and under what authorization context.

Goal
- Define a permission matrix for experiment lifecycle operations and enforce it in Console backend APIs (and where applicable, internal endpoints) with clear error semantics.
- Align with Redwood’s existing Console RBAC roles and enterprise admin patterns.
- Ensure audit log events include enough context for compliance export while avoiding leaking sensitive request identifiers.

Scope (this ticket)
1) Permission model
- Add/confirm the following logical capabilities (names mapped to existing authz framework):
  - experiments:read  (list/get experiment config + status + results)
  - experiments:write (create/update draft config; edit eligibility rules; set guardrails; edit traffic allocations)
  - experiments:operate (start/stop/pause; ramp allocations; acknowledge/override soft-stop banner)
  - experiments:admin (delete; view internal assignment-debug details; break-glass stop if enabled)
- Map capabilities to existing Console roles (initial GA mapping):
  - Viewer / Read-only: experiments:read
  - Operator (aka Release Operator): experiments:read + experiments:operate
  - Editor (aka Config Editor): experiments:read + experiments:write
  - Admin: experiments:* (includes admin)
  - Security Auditor: experiments:read (plus audit log read via separate audit surface; no mutations)

2) Enforcement points
- Console backend endpoints (ENG-9024 surface):
  - POST /experiments -> experiments:write
  - PATCH /experiments/{id} (draft edits, guardrails, allocations) -> experiments:write
  - POST /experiments/{id}/start -> experiments:operate (and validate actor can operate on the target route scope)
  - POST /experiments/{id}/stop -> experiments:operate
  - POST /experiments/{id}/ramp -> experiments:operate
  - DELETE /experiments/{id} -> experiments:admin
  - GET /experiments + GET /experiments/{id} + GET /experiments/{id}/results -> experiments:read
- Internal-only assignment debug endpoint (PR-28596 follow-up): restrict to experiments:admin and internal org users; ensure redaction rules.

3) Audit requirements alignment
- Ensure audit events emitted by ENG-9030 include:
  - actor_id / actor_email (where available)
  - org_id
  - experiment_id
  - route_id(s)
  - action (create/update/start/stop/delete/ramp)
  - authorization context (role/permission check result) in a compact form suitable for export
  - diff summary for updates (no secrets; no raw headers; no customer prompt content)
- Decision: Do not emit audit events for permission-denied attempts in GA (too noisy); rely on standard security logs. Revisit if enterprise asks.

4) UX alignment (non-blocking but recommended)
- Provide UI-facing error codes/messages so Console can show consistent copy:
  - EXPERIMENTS_PERMISSION_DENIED (action-specific)
  - EXPERIMENTS_SCOPE_DENIED (user has operate but not for the specific route/project)
- Console should hide/disable Start/Stop/Delete buttons based on permissions, but backend remains source of truth.

Out of scope
- Fine-grained per-route ownership (e.g., route owners can edit only their route) beyond existing org/project scoping.
- Customer-configurable custom roles. (We can support mapping to existing role framework.)
- SIEM export pipeline changes (covered by audit export work; referenced but not implemented here).

Acceptance criteria
- All experiment mutations are gated in backend by RBAC checks with correct capability requirements.
- Read endpoints are gated and do not leak experiment metadata to unauthorized users.
- Integration tests cover the role matrix for the core endpoints (at minimum: viewer, operator, editor, admin).
- Audit events include required actor/org/experiment identifiers and are emitted for successful mutations.
- Security review sign-off from Marcus Lin on capability mapping and debug endpoint gating approach.

Implementation notes
- Use existing authz middleware; avoid duplicating permission logic across handlers.
- Ensure service-to-service calls (Console -> experiment-service/policy engine) are authenticated separately; RBAC is enforced at Console boundary for user actions.
- For stop semantics: allow Admin to stop even if experiment is in a degraded/soft-stopped state; Operator can stop as well.
- For delete: only Admin. We want a high bar since delete complicates audit trails and incident forensics.

Rollout
- Ship behind route-experiments feature flag. RBAC checks should be enabled regardless of flag state for the endpoints when they are registered.
- Validate in staging with test orgs that have different role assignments; confirm audit events appear in audit trail UI.
comments: 2025-02-05 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Drafted permission matrix proposal (read/write/operate/admin) and shared with Marissa + Dylan for confirmation. Biggest open question: should Editor be allowed to Start? Proposal: no; keep Start/Stop with Operator to match release process patterns.

2025-02-07 (Marcus Lin): Security feedback: ensure delete is admin-only; debug endpoint must be explicitly internal + admin and redact hash inputs that could include customer identifiers. Also prefer standardized error codes for permission failures.
2025-02-10 (Dylan Brooks): +1 to separating write vs operate. We’ve seen too many accidental ramps when edit access is broad. Please ensure ramp endpoint uses operate as well (not write).

2025-02-14 (Chloe Martin): Backend endpoints are landing in ENG-9024 branch. Please hook RBAC middleware at router layer so we don’t miss new endpoints later. Also confirm results endpoint is protected (it’s easy to forget since it’s read-only).

2025-02-18 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Implemented RBAC checks for create/update/start/stop/delete/ramp; added integration tests for viewer/operator/editor/admin. Open item: how to represent authorization context in audit events without expanding schema too much; coordinating with Kevin Osei/ENG-9030.

2025-03-03 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Wired audit context fields (role + capability) into audit payload for successful mutations. No audit event for denied attempts per decision (noise). Added error code EXPERIMENTS_PERMISSION_DENIED with action in message for UI mapping.

2025-03-11 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure on-call can still stop experiments during incident response. Confirmed: Operator can stop; Admin can stop + delete. Break-glass handled via existing Admin escalation process.

2025-03-20 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Addressed review feedback: tightened delete permission, added explicit gating for internal debug endpoint, and added test coverage for scope-denied case (operate allowed at org but restricted by project scope).

2025-03-28 (Chloe Martin): Marking done. Verified in staging with two test users: Viewer cannot see Start/Stop controls; Operator can Start/Stop/Ramp but cannot edit variants; Editor can edit draft but cannot Start; Admin can do all. Audit events show actor + experiment_id + action and include permission context.
